title: Affine fibre-product consequence of a finite Galois tensor decomposition
statement: Let L be a field [def-pc-field-extension], E/L a finite Galois extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] with group Q = Aut_L(E), and let phi : E tensor_L E \to product_{q in Q} E be the L-algebra isomorphism sending a tensor a tensor b to (a q(b))_q. For pi : Spec E \to Spec L [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the fibre product W = Spec E x_{Spec L} Spec E [def-pc-fibre-product] is isomorphic over Spec E (via the first projection) to the finite coproduct of copies of Spec E indexed by Q; on the q-th component the first projection is the identity and the second projection is Spec q.

source.place: Tag 03SF, finite etale objects under a finite Galois extension (tensor decomposition and the resulting disjoint-union description)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with R=L and A=B=E: W is Spec(E tensor_L E), and its projections come from a mapsto a tensor 1 and b mapsto 1 tensor b. The inverse of the given L-algebra isomorphism phi induces W = Spec(E tensor_L E) isomorphic to Spec(product_{q in Q} E). By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields], the maps $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{q\in Q}E)$ induced by the coordinate projections are open immersions with pairwise disjoint images covering the spectrum. Morphisms defined separately on these disjoint open pieces glue uniquely, so they exhibit this spectrum as the coproduct of the Q copies of Spec E. On component q, composing the coordinate projection with phi sends a tensor b to a q(b); in particular a tensor 1 maps to a and 1 tensor b maps to q(b). By contravariance, the restrictions of the two projections of W are respectively id_(Spec E) and Spec q. Since Q contains the identity automorphism, the finite-product statement applies also when E=L (one component).
